presentation_documents.preview:
第 1 页：Nanoparticles in an Optical Tweezer COMSOL
第 2 页：Introduction   Optical tweezers use highly focused laser beams to hold and manipulate objects ranging in size from single atoms to bacteria. This model demonstrates an infrared laser trapping SiO 2  nanospheres suspended in water.   The model first computes the electromagnetic forces on a sphere at various positions within the beam waist, then uses particle tracing to investigate how well the tweezer traps nearby nanospheres. Surrogate modeling is used in order to efficiently cover a dense space of particle positions.
